after: A Venture Global project page says the TransCameron Pipeline extends from the Calcasieu Pass LNG facility to near Grand Chenier, Louisiana. The Energy Information Administration lists it as built in conjunction with the Calcasieu Pass LNG Terminal.

The Energy Information Administration project list says this added compression increases deliverability to the Sabine Pass LNG terminal.

The line is the former U-T Offshore System, bought from Enbridge by Delfin's parent company to bring onshore gas to the Delfin floating LNG export project, according to an Argus Media report from November 2015.

A Federal Energy Regulatory Commission order from May 2020 approved a lease that lets Sabine Pipe Line move 300,000 Dth per day of firm capacity on Bridgeline's intrastate system in southern Louisiana. A federal record of decision from 2017 says the Delfin liquefaction facility will reuse the former UTOS and HIOS offshore pipelines and add a 700-foot, 42-inch bypass to connect them.

A Natural Gas Intelligence article says the Coastal Bend Header project would serve Freeport LNG. The Energy Information Administration project list calls the header a Freeport LNG supply line.
A Rigzone article from July 2025 says Delfin has a long-term lease on the High Island Offshore System pipeline from West Cameron block 167 south to the Delfin Deepwater Port site.
The Energy Information Administration project list says the North Baja Xpress expansion on the whole line was designed to deliver feedstock to the Energia Costa Azul LNG export plant.

A Cheniere project page says this 21.5-mile, 48-inch pipeline carries the feed gas that the Corpus Christi liquefaction plant needs to make LNG. An EIA pipeline projects entry says it allows delivery to the Corpus Christi LNG facility.

The SK Pipeline is about 40 miles of new pipe from the Kinder Morgan Tejas mainline to Freeport LNG's pipeline at Stratton Ridge, Texas. A Kinder Morgan press release from 2014 says it was built to carry 320,000 dekatherms per day for SK E&S LNG's share of Freeport LNG exports.

An RBN Energy post from January 2023 says the Gulf Run pipeline carries Haynesville gas to Louisiana LNG export projects and that Golden Pass LNG is its anchor shipper. The Energy Information Administration project list says it connects the Carthage and Perryville hubs to LNG facilities on the Gulf Coast.
The Stratton Ridge expansion was built to feed the Freeport LNG project. A Natural Gas Intelligence article from March 2019 says so.

A 2017 FERC order for the Gulf Coast Southbound Phase I project says Corpus Christi Liquefaction contracted 385,000 Dth per day of the 460,000 Dth per day, with delivery to the Cheniere Corpus Christi Pipeline.

An EIA Today in Energy article from 2021 says the Cameron Extension expansion on Texas Eastern delivers feedgas to the Calcasieu Pass LNG terminal.

A Kinder Morgan fact sheet says the Evangeline Pass Expansion Project supplies up to 1,100,000 dekatherms per day to Venture Global Plaquemines LNG's Gator Express Pipeline.

The Golden Pass Pipeline was made bidirectional to deliver up to 2.5 billion cubic feet per day of feed gas to the Golden Pass LNG export terminal. The Energy Information Administration list describes this work and names the terminal.

The North Baja XPress expansion was designed to deliver feedgas to the Energia Costa Azul LNG export plant in Baja California, according to the Energy Information Administration pipeline projects list. A Federal Energy Regulatory Commission environmental assessment says the Grand Chenier XPress project would provide feed gas to Venture Global's Calcasieu Pass LNG export terminal.

The Energy Information Administration's October 2026 project table lists the Texas Connector as 31 miles of 42-inch pipe to the proposed Port Arthur LNG Phase 2 facility.

A Williams fact sheet from March 2026 says Driftwood Line 200 will connect Woodside's Louisiana LNG export facility to Transco and other pipelines. The Energy Information Administration lists LNG as the demand served.

An Oil and Gas Journal article from February 2021 describes the 48 inch CP Express pipeline from Jasper County, Texas, to the proposed CP2 LNG plant in Cameron Parish, Louisiana.

A Federal Energy Regulatory Commission environmental assessment for the Freeport LNG Train 4 project lists 10.6 miles of 42-inch pipeline as part of the expansion at the Freeport terminal.

Enbridge agreed in January 2022 to expand the Valley Crossing Pipeline to deliver about 720 million cubic feet per day to Texas LNG's export facility in Brownsville, under a 20-year precedent agreement, according to a report from the Energy Job Shop repeating a PG Online article.
Enbridge and Texas LNG agreed in January 2022 to expand Valley Crossing to deliver 720 million cubic feet per day to Texas LNG, with a 10-mile lateral to the terminal, according to Oil & Gas Journal.

The ADCC Pipeline carries gas from the end of the Whistler Pipeline at Agua Dulce to Cheniere's Corpus Christi liquefaction plant. A World Pipelines article from July 2024 says it supports US LNG exports.

A Natural Gas Intelligence article from June 2022 says the Louisiana Energy Gateway would deliver Haynesville gas to industrial corridors and LNG export projects on the Gulf Coast. A Pipeline and Gas Journal report from July 2025 ties the startup to rising Gulf Coast LNG demand.
An Enbridge project page says the Gator Express Meter Project supplies 240,000 dekatherms per day from Texas Eastern Line 40 for delivery to Venture Global's Plaquemines LNG export facility.

Sabine Crossing is a 55.6-mile, 48-inch pipeline that Cheniere proposes to carry gas to the Sabine Pass LNG Terminal. The Federal Energy Regulatory Commission lists it as part of the Sabine Pass Stage 5 Expansion Project in its final environmental impact statement notice.
A Federal Energy Regulatory Commission notice from December 2013 describes the CE FLNG Project as an LNG export plant plus the CE Pipeline interstate pipeline in Plaquemines Parish, Louisiana.
A Natural Gas Intelligence article from April 2024 says the Venice Extension expands the Texas Eastern system to serve the Plaquemines LNG export facility.

The Saguaro Connector carries Permian gas to the Mexican border to feed the Saguaro Energia LNG export plant in Sonora. A trade press report on the 2024 Federal Energy Regulatory Commission approval says the gas is for overseas LNG shipment.

A Texas Railroad Commission approval in March 2023, described by an Arbo property records article, covers a 562-mile line from Midland County to the Golden Pass LNG terminal in Jefferson County, Texas. The October 2026 EIA pipeline projects release lists LNG as the demand served.

A state pipeline lease application from the Alaska Gasline Development Corporation in October 2019 describes the Point Thomson Transmission Line as part of the Alaska LNG project. It would carry gas from Point Thomson to the Alaska LNG gas treatment plant at Prudhoe Bay.

A Federal Energy Regulatory Commission draft environmental impact statement notice from April 2026 lists the compressor stations and meter work on the Creole Trail Pipeline as part of the Sabine Pass Stage 5 Expansion Project. Sabine Crossing is a 55.6-mile, 48-inch pipeline that Cheniere proposes to carry gas to the Sabine Pass LNG Terminal. The Federal Energy Regulatory Commission lists it as part of the Sabine Pass Stage 5 Expansion Project in its final environmental impact statement notice.
The TTC Connector links Tres Palacios Gas Storage to the Freeport LNG export terminal. An Enbridge story from August 2026 says so, and the Energy Information Administration list says the same.

The 178-mile Mustang Mainline runs from Katy to Port Arthur. A Pipeline and Gas Journal article from October 2025 says Sempra Infrastructure is the anchor shipper to supply its Port Arthur LNG Phase 2 project.

A Federal Energy Regulatory Commission court-case page says the 36.3 mile pipeline was authorized to carry gas from the Bradwood Landing LNG terminal to Northwest Pipeline. An Oil and Gas Journal article says the terminal was an import project.

A Sempra Infrastructure page says Cameron Interstate Pipeline links the Cameron LNG terminal in Cameron Parish, Louisiana, to five interstate pipelines. The 2017 expansion added flow toward Cameron LNG.
A December 2025 Arbo Research note says the Plaquemines LNG expansion would get feed gas from the roughly 300 mile Cloud Connector Pipeline in Louisiana.
A Federal Register notice from 2006 lists this 47.8-mile, 36-inch loop in Maryland as part of the Cove Point LNG import terminal expansion. It was an import project, so the export flag is left blank.

A Boardwalk Pipelines press release from October 2025 says the Texas Gateway Project is meant to supply Texas gas to LNG exporters, utilities, and industrial users near Gillis, Louisiana. A 2010 Williams Partners and Florida Gas Transmission press release says the Pascagoula expansion connects the Gulf LNG import terminal at Bayou Casotte to the Mobile Bay Lateral.

Midship was built by Cheniere to ship gas from the SCOOP and STACK plays in Oklahoma to Cheniere LNG facilities on the Gulf Coast. A Pipeline and Gas Journal article from April 2020 says so. Cheniere owns the Sabine Pass and Corpus Christi terminals.
An Enerdata report on the completed Atlantic Sunrise expansion says the project connects Marcellus gas with markets that include the Cove Point LNG export facility in Maryland.

A May 2026 Canada Gazette order for Westcoast's Sunrise expansion says the T-South system already has firm contracts to deliver gas to Woodfibre LNG, a liquefied natural gas export plant in British Columbia expected in service in 2027. The order says deliveries to that plant will need added capacity on the same system.

A Reuters report from July 2023, printed in Pipeline and Gas Journal, says a fire shut part of a Columbia Gas Transmission line in Virginia. That cut gas to Cove Point, which the report calls an LNG export plant, and the Loudoun LNG interconnect on that line went to near zero.

A draft environmental impact statement from the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission for the proposed Gulf LNG Liquefaction Project names the Destin Pipeline Company system. It describes modifications at the Destin Meter Station and bi-directional flow on the Destin line. The terminal is an import terminal, and the liquefaction project was only proposed, so the export flag is left blank.

A planned outage on that segment cut its capacity and forced Freeport LNG to reduce its loadings.

Houston Pipe Line Company LP, which owns this system, is the seller in a gas sale contract with Sabine Pass Liquefaction, LLC, the company that holds export authority for the Sabine Pass LNG terminal. The contract is dated April 1, 2015, and its confirmation is dated October 11, 2017. A Department of Energy filing lists the contract.

An RBN Energy article says Leach XPress and Rayne XPress were built to connect Marcellus and Utica gas to growing Gulf Coast LNG export demand. Leach XPress itself ends at Leach, Kentucky, and the gas then moves south on Columbia Gulf.

A Cheniere press release from December 2014 says Kinder Morgan Tejas Pipeline, Kinder Morgan Texas Pipeline, and Tennessee Gas Pipeline signed 15-year firm transportation deals with Corpus Christi Liquefaction. The service was to supply the Corpus Christi LNG export plant.

Enbridge says its Texas Eastern Transmission pipeline network supplies natural gas to four operating LNG facilities in the Gulf Coast. A Cheniere project page says the 94-mile, 42-inch bidirectional Creole Trail Pipeline connects the Sabine Pass LNG facility with large interstate pipelines. The facility now exports LNG.

Tellurian planned this pipeline to bring Haynesville gas to Southwest Louisiana alongside its Driftwood LNG export project. A Natural Gas Intelligence article from August 2020 says Tellurian deferred it while advancing Driftwood. Driftwood is now the Woodside Louisiana LNG terminal.

A 2018 Oil & Gas Journal report on the project's open season says the line could serve West Coast LNG exports, including through Energia Costa Azul in Baja California, Mexico.
A Natural Gas Intelligence article from April 2021 reports that the CJ Express expansion signed a firm transportation deal with Golden Pass LNG to supply feed gas to its terminal in Texas.

A Natural Gas Intelligence article from August 2017 says the Permian to Katy pipeline was expected to supply gas for LNG export, power generation, petrochemical use, and Mexico exports. No single terminal is named.
A Steelhead LNG release from September 2015 announced a pre-construction agreement with Williams for the Island Gas Connector to supply the proposed Malahat LNG facility on Vancouver Island.

The Energy Information Administration pipeline projects list says the Alberta Xpress project delivers Canadian gas to the ANR system for delivery to LNG facilities on the Gulf Coast.

A Hydrocarbons Technology project page from 2007 says the Point Comfort pipeline would run from the Calhoun LNG terminal to connect to the pipeline system supplying Texas and the Midwest. The terminal was planned as an import plant.

A Pipeline and Gas Journal item from June 2022 relaying Reuters says Kinder Morgan approved the Permian Highway expansion to bring gas to export hubs near Houston as new Gulf Coast LNG plants were proposed.
The Energy Information Administration list describes the 570 MMcf/d Gulf Coast Express compression expansion from Waha to Agua Dulce and lists LNG as the demand served. It names no terminal.

A Natural Gas Intelligence article from April 2018 says the FERC approval of the East-West Project adds laterals to serve Gulf Coast demand including LNG facilities. Two shippers, JERA Energy America and Shell Energy North America, are active in LNG markets.

The filing says the project is meant to give shippers access to downstream markets, including LNG export facilities along the Gulf Coast, and that sustained LNG demand supports the added capacity. The project leases 43 miles of Bull Run Pipeline's 42-inch extension to the Waha Hub, so the tie is to that extension.

The Energy Information Administration pipeline projects list from October 2026 says the Bull Run Extension moves Delaware Basin gas to Waha for delivery to Texas utilities, industrial customers, and the LNG market.

A Natural Gas Intelligence article from the time of the port license says the port will deliver up to 800 MMcf/d through a 16-mile subsea pipeline that feeds into Algonquin's existing HubLine. This ties the HubLine to an import terminal. No source ties the line to LNG exports, so the export flag stays blank.

The Energy Information Administration pipeline projects list for May 2026 gives the demand served as LNG and storage. Pipeline and Gas Journal said in October 2025 that the site is within 25 miles of more than 30 billion cubic feet a day of current and planned LNG demand.

A 2019 Federal Energy Regulatory Commission order on the Freeport LNG Train 4 project says gas for the project arrives at the Stratton Ridge meter station from interconnections that include the Brazoria Interconnector Pipeline.

An article from 2008 says it was first approved to carry regasified gas from the import terminal.

The Mississippi Hub expansion is tied to LNG exports because a Pipeline and Gas Journal article from April 2025 on the FERC approval says the company cites growing demand for LNG exports as a driver. The article also names LNG and power generation demand in the Southeast as the reason for the expansion.

A Business Wire release from August 2015 says the Oregon Pipeline connector is part of the Oregon LNG bi-directional terminal at Warrenton, Oregon, so it would carry gas both to and from the terminal for export.

The Cypress line was proposed to carry vaporized LNG from the Elba Island import terminal in Georgia to Florida. A Natural Gas Intelligence article from April 2001 says Southern Natural Gas filed for this pipeline to take gas from the recommissioned Elba Island import terminal. The flag stays blank because no source found ties the line to LNG exports.

A Kinder Morgan press release from July 2023 calls the Eagle Ford project a critical supply link for growth from power generators, industrial customers, and LNG exporters on its Texas pipeline network.
